name: Sanctuary Glade

stars.name: Sanctuary
stars.notes: Quiet yellow dwarf with minimal sunspot activity, providing remarkably consistent illumination across geological timescales

planets.name: Brightcoal
planets.notes: Scorched inner world with a surface of fused basalt. Spectral analysis reveals exotic crystalline formations.

planets.name: Willowmere
planets.notes: Temperate garden world with vast wetlands and weeping forests. Indigenous amphibian megafauna. Population 2.8 billion in low-density settlements integrated into the landscape.

planets.name: Misthollow
planets.notes: Cool ocean world perpetually shrouded in mist. Extensive kelp forests support a fishing-based economy. Population 740 million in archipelago and platform settlements.

planets.name: Barrowfield
planets.notes: Dry world with ancient fossilized forests visible from orbit. Paleobiology expeditions study its extinct biosphere for clues about the system's evolutionary history.

planets.name: Greygiant
planets.notes: Subdued grey-blue jovian with a spectacular ring system. Two moons host helium-3 extraction facilities.

planets.name: Sleepstone
planets.notes: Distant ice dwarf with a surface of nitrogen frost. Automated deep-space monitoring equipment tracks outer system approaches.

asteroid_belts.name: The Fossil Scatter
asteroid_belts.notes: Asteroid fragments containing fossilized microorganisms, suggesting an ancient disrupted body that once harbored life. Intensively studied by paleoxenobiologists.

stations.name: Glade Station
stations.notes: Primary commerce hub with extensive quarantine facilities. Exports wetland pharmaceuticals and amphibian-derived biological compounds.

stations.name: Mistport
stations.notes: Trade and fishing fleet coordination station. Manages sustainable harvest quotas for Misthollow's kelp forests.

stations.name: Barrowfield Camp
stations.notes: Permanent paleobiology research base studying the planet's extinct biosphere. Findings published in journals across known space.

faction_control.notes: Consensus-based governance emphasizing quiet prosperity and ecological harmony. Known for welcoming refugees and displaced populations from conflict zones.

history: Settled in 2274 by colonists specifically seeking a peaceful, ecologically rich system far from the territorial disputes of the core worlds.
The discovery of fossilized life in the Fossil Scatter in 2289 revealed that the system once hosted at least three living worlds, elevating its scientific significance considerably.
Sanctuary Glade's reputation as a haven has grown steadily, with the Communion accepting over 12 million refugees from the Frontier Wars between 2301 and 2315.
description: Sanctuary Glade is a system that breathes tranquility. Its yellow sun casts steady light across six worlds, two of them verdant and alive. Willowmere is a planet of mists and wetlands, where weeping forests drape their branches into slow-moving rivers and amphibian megafauna—gentle giants the size of houses—wade through marshes that stretch to every horizon. Misthollow lives up to its name: a cool ocean world where fog banks drift across kelp-choked seas and fishing fleets navigate by sonar as much as by sight. Even dead Barrowfield contributes to the system's character, its petrified forests standing as monuments to the life that once was.

The system's culture matches its landscape. The Sanctuary Glade Communion governs through consensus, preferring deliberation over speed, sustainability over growth. Colonists came here seeking peace, and peace is what they built. The Communion's open-door refugee policy has made it one of the most culturally diverse systems in the sector, with communities from dozens of conflict-scarred worlds finding shelter among Willowmere's wetlands and Misthollow's misty archipelagos. This generosity has earned the system deep goodwill—and occasionally drawn the attention of those who would exploit it.

The Fossil Scatter tells a story that haunts the system's scientists. Fossilized microorganisms in the asteroid belt, combined with Barrowfield's petrified forests, suggest that life once flourished on three worlds here—not two. What catastrophe sterilized Barrowfield while leaving Willowmere and Misthollow untouched? The leading theory involves a massive impact that stripped Barrowfield's atmosphere, but the evidence remains incomplete. Some researchers at Barrowfield Camp believe the answer lies deeper underground, in strata not yet excavated. The past, in Sanctuary Glade, is never quite finished revealing its secrets.
